title: Exec brief: Ops runway & decision requests for runtime optimization investments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Prepare a concise exec-facing packet that summarizes the operational runway for the next 90 days of runtime and serving investments, frames three decision requests (budget reallocation, canary expansion, and fallback SLA policy), and provides measurable success criteria for each request. This packet will be used in the monthly exec readout and as the basis for a QBR ask if prioritization is required. The focus is on balancing unit cost reduction (quantization, batching) with latency SLOs and rollout safety for Dedicated and Hosted customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) One-pager that clearly states 3 decision requests and associated asks (dollars, engineering effort, and timing)
2) Risk register with mitigation lanes and rollback criteria for each canary expansion
3) Run-rate savings model (cost per 1M tokens) under conservative and optimistic scenarios
4) Routed and reviewed by Eng leads and Finance, with sign-off captured in comments
decision_requests: Budget reallocation: Move $250k from 'validation infra' to 'runtime kernel optimization' for H2; expected payback within 5 quarters based on 20% unit-cost reduction for batchy workloads
Canary expansion: Approve staged canary for continuous batching on Dedicated pools (start: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50%) with predefined rollback thresholds for P95 latency and error rate

SLA fallback policy: Approve automated fallback chain that routes to cost-optimized model variant when latency SLOs are at risk (requires policy-level sign-off and a short window of manual override for 72 hours)
risks: Latency regressions after aggressive quantization leading to customer complaints
Engineering dependency: kernel upstream changes may slip by 2-4 weeks, impacting canary schedule
Financial: projected savings may not materialize if traffic distribution shifts away from batch-friendly patterns
Compliance: Private deployments require additional testing for KMS interactions when changing model runtimes
